before.title: The barotropic fluid equations in enthalpy form are symmetric hyperbolic with positive principal symbol
before.statement:
Let a perfect-fluid model with smooth equation of state $p=p(\epsilon)$ satisfy
$\epsilon+p>0$ and $0<p'(\epsilon)<1$ on an open interval $J$, let
$r:J\to r(J)$ and $c_s=\sqrt{p'}$ be the enthalpy variable and sound speed of
[[def-gr-barotropic-enthalpy-variable]], and let $D,\vartheta,a^b,h^{ab}$
denote the comoving derivative, expansion, acceleration and rest-space
projection of [[def-gr-perfect-fluid-matter-model]]. Then:

**(a)** the perfect-fluid equations
$D\epsilon+(\epsilon+p)\vartheta=0$, $(\epsilon+p)a^b+h^{ba}\partial_ap=0$ are
equivalent to
$$D r+c_s\,\vartheta=0,\qquad D n^b+c_s\,h^{ba}\partial_a r=0 ,$$
and the stress-energy tensor
$T^{ab}=(\epsilon+p)n^an^b+pg^{ab}$ is divergence-free exactly when these
equations hold;

**(b)** in every orthonormal frame $(n,e_1,e_2,e_3)$ at a point, the principal
symbol of the system (a) in the variables $(r,n^1,n^2,n^3)$ at a covector
$\zeta=\zeta_0n^\flat+\zeta_\perp$ is the symmetric matrix
$$A(\zeta)=\begin{pmatrix}\zeta_0&c_s\zeta_\perp^{\mathsf T}\\ c_s\zeta_\perp&\zeta_0 I_3\end{pmatrix};$$
its eigenvalues are $\zeta_0$ (multiplicity two) and
$\zeta_0\pm c_s|\zeta_\perp|$ (multiplicity one each); consequently $A(\zeta)$
is positive definite for every future-directed timelike covector $\zeta$
(because $\zeta_0>|\zeta_\perp|$ and $c_s<1$);

**(c)** consequently the combined Einstein-fluid system, with the reduced
Einstein equation in the harmonic gauge, is a first-order quasilinear symmetric
hyperbolic system with positive definite time matrix, coupled only through
zeroth-order terms in the first derivatives of the metric.

Assume Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]) for the enthalpy integral. Fix a smooth EOS $p=p(\epsilon)$ on an open interval $J$ satisfying $\epsilon+p>0$ and $0<p'(\epsilon)<1$. Fix the integration reference in the enthalpy variable $r$ of [[def-gr-barotropic-enthalpy-variable]], and put $c_s=\sqrt{p'}$. Let $u$ be the future unit fluid velocity, $D=\nabla_u$, $\vartheta=\nabla_a u^a$, $a=\nabla_u u$ and $\Pi^{ab}=g^{ab}+u^au^b$ ([[def-gr-perfect-fluid-matter-model]]). Then:

**(a)** The full fluid equations are equivalent to
$$Dr+c_s\vartheta=0,\qquad \nabla_u u^b+c_s\Pi^{ba}\partial_ar=0.$$
The fluid stress $T^{ab}=(\epsilon+p)u^au^b+pg^{ab}$ is divergence-free precisely when these fluid equations hold.

**(b)** For variations $\eta=(\delta r,\delta u)$ with $g(u,\delta u)=0$, the smooth symmetric principal bilinear form at a covector $\zeta$ is
$$Q_\zeta(\eta,\eta')=\zeta(u)\left[\delta r\delta r'+g(\delta u,\delta u')\right]+c_s\left[\delta r\zeta(\delta u')+\delta r'\zeta(\delta u)\right].$$
For every timelike covector positively evaluated on future timelike vectors, it is positive definite. In a rest orthonormal basis it has eigenvalues $\zeta(u)$ twice and $\zeta(u)\pm c_s|\zeta_\perp|$, where $\zeta=-\zeta(u)u^\flat+\zeta_\perp$. Smooth velocity coordinates turn this bilinear form into actual smooth symmetric coefficient matrices.

**(c)** Appending the harmonic reduced Einstein metric block gives a smooth coupled first-order symmetric hyperbolic family on a local open admissible state set, with zeroth-order coupling in derivatives of the first-order variables. In an initially orthogonal chart, complete fluid data are $(\epsilon_0,v_0)$ with $h(v_0,v_0)<1$, or the corresponding bundle velocity $U_0=W_0(N+v_0)$, $W_0=(1-h(v_0,v_0))^{-1/2}$ in $\mathbb RN\oplus T\Sigma$. They initialize $r=r(\epsilon_0)$, $u^0=W_0$ and $u^i=W_0v_0^i$. Normalization is enforced by reconstruction, and a reduced solution recovers the full fluid equations and conserved stress before imposing Einstein's unreduced equations. Every full fluid solution extracts to the same system. No vanishing-sound-speed or dust conclusion is asserted.

citations.quote:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice for the integral below
([[def-countable-choice]]). Let a perfect-fluid model on a Lorentzian manifold
be given with smooth equation of state $p=p(\epsilon)$ defined on an open
interval $J\subseteq\mathbb R$, with $\epsilon+p(\epsilon)>0$ and
$p'(\epsilon)>0$ for all $\epsilon\in J$
([[def-gr-perfect-fluid-matter-model]]). Fix a base point
$\epsilon_*\in J$ and define the **barotropic enthalpy variable**
$$r:J\to\mathbb R,\qquad r(\epsilon):=\int_{\epsilon_*}^{\epsilon}\frac{\sqrt{p'(z)}}{z+p(z)}\,dz .$$
The integrand is continuous on $J$ ([[thm-continuous-implies-integrable]]), so
$r$ is well defined and $C^1$ with $r'(\epsilon)=\sqrt{p'(\epsilon)}/(\epsilon+p(\epsilon))>0$
([[cor-ftc-integral-function-differentiable-almost-everywhere]]); hence $r$
maps $J$ diffeomorphically onto the open interval $r(J)$, and we write
$\epsilon(r)$ for its inverse and $c_s:=\sqrt{p'}$ for the **sound-speed
function**, so that $r'(\epsilon)=c_s(\epsilon)/(\epsilon+p(\epsilon))$ and
$c_s\in(0,1)$ when $0<p'<1$ is assumed.

The definition and the two displayed equivalences are the form in which the
fluid system is fed into [[lem-gr-barotropic-fluid-symmetric-hyperbolic-system]];
no existence theorem is asserted here.

Let $M$ and $N$ be smooth manifolds, let $F:M\to N$ be a map, let $p\in M$ and
let $r\in\mathbb N_0\cup\{\infty\}$, where $\mathbb N_0=\{0,1,2,\ldots\}$.
For $m,q\in\mathbb N_0$ and an open set $E\subseteq\mathbb R^m$, a map
$g:E\to\mathbb R^q$ is **of class $C^r$** as follows. When $m=0$, every such
map is declared $C^r$. When $m\ge1$, each component $g_l$ with $l<q$ must be
$C^r$ in the sense of
[[def-ck-and-multi-index-notation-in-several-variables]]; when $q=0$ this
component condition is vacuous.
Suppose $F$ is continuous at $p$. Then $F$ is **of class $C^r$ at $p$** when
there are smooth charts $(U,\varphi)$ of $M$ at $p$ and $(V,\psi)$ of $N$ at
$F(p)$ with $F(U)\subseteq V$ such that the coordinate representative

$$\psi\circ F\circ\varphi^{-1}:\varphi(U)\longrightarrow\psi(V)$$

([[def-coordinate-representation-of-a-map]]) is of class $C^r$ on a
neighbourhood of $\varphi(p)$ in this componentwise Euclidean sense. By
[[lem-chart-independence-of-c-r-smoothness]], this condition is independent of
the chosen charts: if one such representative is $C^r$, then every one is, so
"some charts" may be read as "any charts". A map is **$C^r$ on an open set**
$W\subseteq M$ when it is continuous on $W$ and $C^r$ at every point of $W$. A
map that is $C^r$ for every finite $r$ — equivalently $C^\infty$ — is called
**smooth**; the term **$C^r$ map between smooth manifolds** is reserved for the
case where $F$ is continuous and the representative condition holds at every
point of $M$.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with
metric-selected connection $\nabla$ and let $U\subseteq M$ be a nonempty open
matter domain ([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]],
[[prop-an-open-subset-of-a-smooth-manifold-has-a-canonical-restricted-smooth-structure]]).

**(a) Dust.** Let $(\rho,u,T)$ be a dust model on $U$
([[def-gr-dust-matter-model]]). Then

$$\nabla^aT_{ab}=0\ \text{on }U\qquad\Longleftrightarrow\qquad \nabla_a(\rho u^a)=0\ \text{and}\ u^a\nabla_au^b=0\ \text{on }U .$$

**(b) Perfect fluid.** Let $(\varepsilon,p,n,T)$ be a perfect-fluid model on
$U$ with comoving derivative $D$, expansion $\vartheta$, acceleration $a$ and
projection $h$ ([[def-gr-perfect-fluid-matter-model]]). Then

$$\nabla^aT_{ab}=0\ \text{on }U\qquad\Longleftrightarrow\qquad D\varepsilon+(\varepsilon+p)\vartheta=0\quad\text{and}\quad (\varepsilon+p)a^b+h^{ba}\partial_ap=0\ \text{on }U .$$

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold, let $\bar g$
be a smooth background metric with Levi-Civita connection $\bar\nabla$, and let
$H^a=g^{bc}(\Gamma^a{}_{bc}-\bar\Gamma^a{}_{bc})$ be the harmonic-gauge vector
of [[def-gr-harmonic-gauge-and-reduced-equations]]. Then:

**(a) [principal part]** Let $\hat g$ be a smooth Lorentzian metric on an open
set $U\subseteq M$ and let $h$ be a smooth symmetric covariant $2$-tensor on
$U$. The derivative at $\hat g$ in the direction $h$ of the operator
$g\mapsto\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}[g]-\bar\nabla_{(a}H_{b)}[g]$ equals
$$-\tfrac12\hat g^{cd}\,\bar\nabla_c\bar\nabla_d h_{ab}+L_{ab}(h,\bar\nabla h;\hat g,\bar g),$$
where $L$ is a smooth expression linear in $h$ and its first
$\bar\nabla$-derivatives with coefficients built from $\hat g,\hat g^{-1},\bar g$
and the background curvature. In particular the principal symbol is
$-\tfrac12\hat g^{cd}\xi_c\xi_d$ times the identity on the metric slot at every
covector $\xi$.

**(b) [first-order reduction]** Fix a chart $(x^0,x^1,x^2,x^3)$ with
$x^0=t$. Introduce the metric variables
$$u:=\bigl(g_{ab},\ p_{ab}:=\bar\nabla_0g_{ab},\ q_{abi}:=\bar\nabla_ig_{ab}\bigr)$$
(symmetry in $a,b$ understood) and the relation variables $\bar\nabla_0g_{ab}-p_{ab}=0$, $\bar\nabla_0q_{abi}-\bar\nabla_ip_{ab}=0$. Then the reduced Einstein equation can be solved for the second time derivatives in the form
$$\bar\nabla_0p_{ab}=-(g^{00})^{-1}\Bigl[2g^{0i}\bar\nabla_ip_{ab}+g^{ij}\bar\nabla_iq_{abj}+R_{ab}(u,\bar\nabla u;\bar g)\Bigr],$$
and the resulting first-order system for $u$ is symmetric hyperbolic on every
region where $g^{00}<0$ and the spatial block $(g^{ij})$ is positive definite:
the coefficient of $\bar\nabla_0u$ is the block diagonal
$\operatorname{diag}(I,-g^{00}I,g^{ij}I)$ (on the three slots
$g,p,q$), which is positive definite there, and the coefficients of the spatial
derivatives are symmetric.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold and let
$p\in M$ ([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]). The cotangent space $T_p^*M$ is
the algebraic dual of $T_pM$ ([[def-algebraic-dual-and-linear-functional]]).

**Musical isomorphisms.** Define the **flat map**

$$\flat_p:T_pM\longrightarrow T_p^*M,\qquad \flat_p(v):=g_p(v,\cdot),$$

so that $\flat_p(v)(w)=g_p(v,w)$; it is $\mathbb R$-linear by bilinearity of
$g_p$. Its kernel is $\{v:g_p(v,w)=0\text{ for all }w\}=\{0\}$ because $g_p$ is
nondegenerate, and $\dim_{\mathbb R}T_pM=\dim_{\mathbb R}T_p^*M=4$ since the
coordinate derivations of a chart form a basis of $T_pM$
([[thm-coordinate-derivations-form-a-basis-of-the-tangent-space]]); hence
$\flat_p$ is a linear isomorphism and has an inverse
$\sharp_p:T_p^*M\to T_pM$.

**Inverse metric.** The **inverse metric** at $p$ is the symmetric bilinear form

$$g_p^{-1}:T_p^*M\times T_p^*M\longrightarrow\mathbb R,\qquad g_p^{-1}(\alpha,\beta):=g_p(\sharp_p\alpha,\sharp_p\beta).$$

It is symmetric because $g_p$ is, and it is nondegenerate: if
$g_p^{-1}(\alpha,\beta)=0$ for all $\beta$, then $g_p(\sharp_p\alpha,\cdot)=0$,
so $\sharp_p\alpha=0$ and hence $\alpha=0$.

**Components in a chart.** Let $(U,x)$ be a smooth chart and
$g_{ab}(q)=g_q(\partial_a|_q,\partial_b|_q)$ the components of $g$; let
$dx^a|_q$ be the differential of the coordinate function $x^a$ at $q$
([[def-differential-of-a-smooth-map]]), so that
$dx^a|_q(\partial_b|_q)=\partial_b|_q(x^a)=\delta^a{}_b$. Define the components
of the inverse metric in this chart by

$$g^{ab}(q):=g_q^{-1}\bigl(dx^a|_q,\,dx^b|_q\bigr),\qquad q\in U,$$

so that $\sharp_q(dx^a|_q)=\sum_bg^{ab}(q)\,\partial_b|_q$; equivalently
$(g^{ab}(q))$ is the inverse matrix of $(g_{ab}(q))$ at every $q$, that is

$$g^{ac}(q)\,g_{cb}(q)=\delta^a{}_b=\delta^c{}_bg^{ab}(q),$$

because $g_q(\sharp_qdx^a|_q,\partial_c|_q)=dx^a|_q(\partial_c|_q)=\delta^a{}_c$
and also $g_q(\sharp_qdx^a|_q,\partial_c|_q)=\sum_bg^{ab}(q)g_{bc}(q)$. In
particular $g^{ab}=g^{ba}$. The components $g^{ab}$ depend smoothly on $q$;
this is proved in [[lem-gr-inverse-metric-is-smooth]].

**Raising, lowering and metric trace.** Let $A$ be a smooth symmetric covariant
$2$-tensor field on an open set $V\subseteq M$
([[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]]). At each $p\in V$ define the
endomorphism

$$A^\sharp_p:T_pM\to T_pM,\qquad A^\sharp_p(v):=\sharp_p\bigl(A_p(v,\cdot)\bigr),$$

characterized by $g_p(A^\sharp_p(v),w)=A_p(v,w)$ for all $w\in T_pM$; it is
self-adjoint for $g_p$ because $A_p$ is symmetric. Its **metric trace** is

$$\operatorname{tr}_g(A)(p):=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(A^\sharp_p\bigr)$$

with the trace of an endomorphism as in [[def-trace-of-an-endomorphism]]. In a
chart the raised, mixed and doubly raised components are

$$A^{ab}:=g^{ac}g^{bd}A_{cd},\qquad A^a{}_b:=g^{ac}A_{cb},\qquad\text{and}\qquad \operatorname{tr}_g(A)=g^{ab}A_{ab},$$

the last identity obtained by evaluating in a $g_p$-orthonormal basis
$(e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$, where $g_p(e_a,e_b)=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)_{ab}$ by
[[lem-timelike-cone-has-two-convex-components]] so that
$g^{ab}A_{ab}=\sum_a g^{aa}A_{aa}=-A(e_0,e_0)+A(e_1,e_1)+A(e_2,e_2)+A(e_3,e_3)$,
which is the trace of the endomorphism $v\mapsto\sharp_p(A_p(v,\cdot))$ in that
basis. All these operations are pointwise and depend only on $g$, $A$ and the
duality pairing, not on a chart.

**Conventions.** Raising and lowering apply to one index at a time and preserve
index order; $A_{ab}$, $A^a{}_b$ and $A^{ab}$ denote the same tensor $A$ with
indices positioned by $g$. The musical isomorphisms and the inverse metric are
defined for every smooth Lorentzian four-manifold of this library; no choice
principle is used in this definition, every ingredient being pointwise linear
algebra over $\mathbb R$ together with the pointwise nondegeneracy of $g_p$.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]) and let $\nabla$ be an affine connection
on $M$ ([[def-affine-connection-on-a-smooth-manifold]]). Smooth vector fields
are smooth sections of the tangent bundle
([[def-smooth-vector-field-as-a-tangent-bundle-section]]); as there, their use
rests on the canonical smooth structure of $TM$, which assumes the axiom
$\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ of [[def-countable-choice]]. This is the only use of that
axiom in this definition.

**(a) Metric compatibility.** The connection $\nabla$ is **$g$-compatible**, or
**compatible with the metric** $g$, when for all smooth vector fields $X,Y,Z$ on
$M$ the identity of smooth functions

$$X\bigl(g(Y,Z)\bigr)=g(\nabla_XY,Z)+g(Y,\nabla_XZ)$$

holds on $M$. Here $g(Y,Z)$ is the smooth function $p\mapsto g_p(Y_p,Z_p)$ and
$X$ acts on functions as a derivation; the identity uses only the action of
$\nabla$ on vector fields and requires no extension of $\nabla$ to tensor
fields. When such an extension is available, this identity is the statement
$\nabla_Xg=0$, and the compatibility of $\nabla$ with the inverse metric
$g^{-1}$ follows; neither statement is part of this definition.

**(b) Torsion freedom.** The **torsion** of $\nabla$ is the tangent-valued
$2$-tensor $T(X,Y)=\nabla_XY-\nabla_YX-[X,Y]$ of
[[def-torsion-tensor-of-an-affine-connection]], with bracket as in
[[def-lie-bracket-of-smooth-vector-fields]]. The connection is **torsion-free**
when $T(X,Y)=0$ for all smooth $X,Y$, that is, when
$\nabla_XY-\nabla_YX=[X,Y]$ identically.

**(c) Metric-selected connections.** A **metric-selected connection** for
$(M,g)$ is an affine connection on $M$ that is both torsion-free and
$g$-compatible. Equivalently, it is an element of the class

$$\operatorname{LC}(M,g):=\{\nabla:\nabla\text{ is an affine connection on }M,\ \nabla\text{ is torsion-free and }g\text{-compatible}\}.$$

The name records that the pair of conditions selects the connection out of all
affine connections; it is the pair of conditions imposed on the connection that
conventional general relativity uses, and the connection so selected is called
the **Levi–Civita connection** of $g$.

Let $M$ be a smooth four-manifold without boundary and let $g$ be a smooth
symmetric covariant $2$-tensor field on $M$ such that $g_p$ is nondegenerate at
every $p\in M$ ([[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]],
[[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]]). This holds in particular
when $(M,g,N)$ is a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold and $g$ is
its metric ([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]). For smooth vector fields
$X,Y,Z$ put

$$K(X,Y,Z):=X\bigl(g(Y,Z)\bigr)+Y\bigl(g(Z,X)\bigr)-Z\bigl(g(X,Y)\bigr)+g([X,Y],Z)+g([Z,X],Y)-g([Y,Z],X),$$

with brackets as in [[def-lie-bracket-of-smooth-vector-fields]].

**(a) Existence and formulas.** There is exactly one affine connection
$\nabla$ on $M$ ([[def-affine-connection-on-a-smooth-manifold]]) satisfying

$$2g(\nabla_XY,Z)=K(X,Y,Z)\qquad\text{for all smooth }X,Y,Z .$$

It is torsion-free and $g$-compatible, so it is a metric-selected connection
for $(M,g)$ ([[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]]); in every smooth chart its
Christoffel symbols are

$$\Gamma^a{}_{bc}=\tfrac12\,g^{ad}\bigl(\partial_bg_{dc}+\partial_cg_{bd}-\partial_dg_{bc}\bigr),$$

with $g^{ad}$ the inverse-metric components
([[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]],
[[def-christoffel-symbols-of-an-affine-connection]]).

**(b) Uniqueness.** If an affine connection $\nabla'$ on $M$ is torsion-free
and $g$-compatible, then $\nabla'=\nabla$. Consequently the class
$\operatorname{LC}(M,g)$ of metric-selected connections has exactly one
element; it is the **Levi–Civita connection** of $g$.

**(c) Induced derivative on tensor fields.** Let $\nabla^*$ be the dual
connection on $T^*M$ and let the product connection of
[[def-product-connection-on-tensor-and-hom-bundles]] act on the tensor bundles
of [[def-gr-tensor-fields-and-components]]. Then, in every smooth chart, for
every smooth tensor field $T$ of type $(r,s)$,

$$T^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s;c}=\partial_cT^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s}+\sum_{i=1}^{r}\Gamma^{a_i}{}_{dc}\,T^{a_1\cdots d\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s}-\sum_{j=1}^{s}\Gamma^{d}{}_{b_jc}\,T^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots d\cdots b_s},$$

where the slot marked $d$ replaces the named index; this derivative commutes
with every contraction in the sense of [[def-contraction-of-a-mixed-tensor]],
and it annihilates the metric and the inverse metric:

$$g_{ab;c}=0,\qquad g^{ab}{}_{;c}=0 .$$

derivations.claim: (The change of variables and (a).) By [L1] the maps $\epsilon\leftrightarrow r$ are smooth and invertible. Computing $Dr$ and $c_s\partial_ar$ with the chain rule as in [L2] and substituting into the fluid equations gives the displayed system; conversely, the same identities with $\epsilon$ as a function of $r$ recover the original equations. Divergence-freeness is [L3]. This is (a).

(The principal symbol (b).) The system (a) has the form (scalar equation for $r$) plus (vector equation for $n$): $n^\mu\partial_\mu r+c_s\,\partial_\mu n^\mu+\ldots=0$ and $n^\mu\partial_\mu n^b+c_s\,h^{ba}\partial_ar=0$ plus zeroth-order (connection) terms. Replacing $\partial_\mu$ by $\zeta_\mu$ in the leading terms and evaluating in a rest frame where $n=\partial_0$, so that $h$ projects onto the spatial directions, gives the displayed $A(\zeta)$: the first row is $(\zeta_0,c_s\zeta_\perp^{\mathsf T})$ and the spatial block is $\zeta_0I_3$ with the symmetric off-diagonal $c_s\zeta_\perp$. Its eigenvalues are computed from the block structure: on the space orthogonal to $\zeta_\perp$ the matrix is $\zeta_0I$; on the two-dimensional span of $(1,0)$ and $(0,\hat\zeta_\perp)$ it is the symmetric $2\times2$ matrix with diagonal $\zeta_0$ and off-diagonal $c_s|\zeta_\perp|$, with eigenvalues $\zeta_0\pm c_s|\zeta_\perp|$.

(Positivity.) For future-directed timelike $\zeta$, [L5] gives $\zeta_0>|\zeta_\perp|\ge0$; since $0<c_s<1$, $\zeta_0-c_s|\zeta_\perp|>\zeta_0-|\zeta_\perp|>0$, and the other eigenvalues $\zeta_0,\zeta_0+c_s|\zeta_\perp|$ are positive as well. Hence $A(\zeta)$ is positive definite. This is (b).

(The coupled system (c).) By [L4] the metric block is symmetric with positive time matrix and its coupling to the matter is zeroth order; by (b) the fluid block has positive time matrix; the spatial symbols of both blocks are symmetric and the cross-coupling carries no derivatives. Hence the combined system is symmetric hyperbolic with positive definite time matrix. This is (c). [step 1.2, step 2.1, L4, algebra] ∎



- **Role.** Clause (c) verifies the matter hypothesis of [[thm-gr-local-geometric-development]] for the strict interior-fluid branch; the hypothesis $0<p'<1$ is used exactly in (b), and its failure is analyzed in the counterexample of the examples page.

boundaries.reason: No empty set, empty family or empty index range is formed: the quantified objects (points, fields, mode families, data sets) are nonempty by the hypotheses, and the proofs never split off an empty case.
The value zero is not a distinguished boundary of this claim: no step divides by a quantity that can vanish and no separate zero case is required.
No cardinality-one case is separated: the arguments treat general finite or countable families and the one-element case is included without special treatment.

The hypotheses exclude degenerate configurations: the metric is Lorentzian/nondegenerate, the time matrix or coefficient is positive definite, velocity fields are unit and nonzero where required, and no degenerate limit is claimed.
The assertions are local in open domains around the initial surface or open time intervals, and no endpoint behaviour (completeness, boundary extension or endpoint regularity) is claimed.
No nonconstructive selection from a family is made: the argument uses the objects named in the Given clause and the supplied maps, with at most finite choices.

boundaries.evidence: step 1.1 substitutes the chain-rule identities into the fluid equations to obtain the $r$-system, the forward direction of the stated equivalence.

([[def-gr-perfect-fluid-matter-model]]). Fix a base point
$\epsilon_*\in J$ and define the **barotropic enthalpy variable**

([[cor-ftc-integral-function-differentiable-almost-everywhere]]); hence $r$
maps $J$ diffeomorphically onto the open interval $r(J)$, and we write

Let $M$ and $N$ be smooth manifolds, let $F:M\to N$ be a map, let $p\in M$ and
let $r\in\mathbb N_0\cup\{\infty\}$, where $\mathbb N_0=\{0,1,2,\ldots\}$.

$g:E\to\mathbb R^q$ is **of class $C^r$** as follows. When $m=0$, every such
map is declared $C^r$. When $m\ge1$, each component $g_l$ with $l<q$ must be
$C^r$ in the sense of
[[def-ck-and-multi-index-notation-in-several-variables]]; when $q=0$ this
component condition is vacuous.
Suppose $F$ is continuous at $p$. Then $F$ is **of class $C^r$ at $p$** when
there are smooth charts $(U,\varphi)$ of $M$ at $p$ and $(V,\psi)$ of $N$ at
$F(p)$ with $F(U)\subseteq V$ such that the coordinate representative

$$\psi\circ F\circ\varphi^{-1}:\varphi(U)\longrightarrow\psi(V)$$

([[def-coordinate-representation-of-a-map]]) is of class $C^r$ on a
neighbourhood of $\varphi(p)$ in this componentwise Euclidean sense. By
[[lem-chart-independence-of-c-r-smoothness]], this condition is independent of
the chosen charts: if one such representative is $C^r$, then every one is, so
"some charts" may be read as "any charts". A map is **$C^r$ on an open set**
$W\subseteq M$ when it is continuous on $W$ and $C^r$ at every point of $W$. A
map that is $C^r$ for every finite $r$ — equivalently $C^\infty$ — is called
**smooth**; the term **$C^r$ map between smooth manifolds** is reserved for the
case where $F$ is continuous and the representative condition holds at every
point of $M$.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with
metric-selected connection $\nabla$ and let $U\subseteq M$ be a nonempty open
matter domain ([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]],
[[prop-an-open-subset-of-a-smooth-manifold-has-a-canonical-restricted-smooth-structure]]).

**(a) Dust.** Let $(\rho,u,T)$ be a dust model on $U$
([[def-gr-dust-matter-model]]). Then

$$\nabla^aT_{ab}=0\ \text{on }U\qquad\Longleftrightarrow\qquad \nabla_a(\rho u^a)=0\ \text{and}\ u^a\nabla_au^b=0\ \text{on }U .$$

**(b) Perfect fluid.** Let $(\varepsilon,p,n,T)$ be a perfect-fluid model on
$U$ with comoving derivative $D$, expansion $\vartheta$, acceleration $a$ and
projection $h$ ([[def-gr-perfect-fluid-matter-model]]). Then

$$\nabla^aT_{ab}=0\ \text{on }U\qquad\Longleftrightarrow\qquad D\varepsilon+(\varepsilon+p)\vartheta=0\quad\text{and}\quad (\varepsilon+p)a^b+h^{ba}\partial_ap=0\ \text{on }U .$$

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold, let $\bar g$
be a smooth background metric with Levi-Civita connection $\bar\nabla$, and let
$H^a=g^{bc}(\Gamma^a{}_{bc}-\bar\Gamma^a{}_{bc})$ be the harmonic-gauge vector
of [[def-gr-harmonic-gauge-and-reduced-equations]]. Then:

**(a) [principal part]** Let $\hat g$ be a smooth Lorentzian metric on an open
set $U\subseteq M$ and let $h$ be a smooth symmetric covariant $2$-tensor on
$U$. The derivative at $\hat g$ in the direction $h$ of the operator
$g\mapsto\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}[g]-\bar\nabla_{(a}H_{b)}[g]$ equals
$$-\tfrac12\hat g^{cd}\,\bar\nabla_c\bar\nabla_d h_{ab}+L_{ab}(h,\bar\nabla h;\hat g,\bar g),$$
where $L$ is a smooth expression linear in $h$ and its first
$\bar\nabla$-derivatives with coefficients built from $\hat g,\hat g^{-1},\bar g$
and the background curvature. In particular the principal symbol is
$-\tfrac12\hat g^{cd}\xi_c\xi_d$ times the identity on the metric slot at every
covector $\xi$.

**(b) [first-order reduction]** Fix a chart $(x^0,x^1,x^2,x^3)$ with
$x^0=t$. Introduce the metric variables
$$u:=\bigl(g_{ab},\ p_{ab}:=\bar\nabla_0g_{ab},\ q_{abi}:=\bar\nabla_ig_{ab}\bigr)$$
(symmetry in $a,b$ understood) and the relation variables $\bar\nabla_0g_{ab}-p_{ab}=0$, $\bar\nabla_0q_{abi}-\bar\nabla_ip_{ab}=0$. Then the reduced Einstein equation can be solved for the second time derivatives in the form
$$\bar\nabla_0p_{ab}=-(g^{00})^{-1}\Bigl[2g^{0i}\bar\nabla_ip_{ab}+g^{ij}\bar\nabla_iq_{abj}+R_{ab}(u,\bar\nabla u;\bar g)\Bigr],$$
and the resulting first-order system for $u$ is symmetric hyperbolic on every
region where $g^{00}<0$ and the spatial block $(g^{ij})$ is positive definite:
the coefficient of $\bar\nabla_0u$ is the block diagonal
$\operatorname{diag}(I,-g^{00}I,g^{ij}I)$ (on the three slots
$g,p,q$), which is positive definite there, and the coefficients of the spatial
derivatives are symmetric.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold and let
$p\in M$ ([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]). The cotangent space $T_p^*M$ is
the algebraic dual of $T_pM$ ([[def-algebraic-dual-and-linear-functional]]).

**Musical isomorphisms.** Define the **flat map**

$$\flat_p:T_pM\longrightarrow T_p^*M,\qquad \flat_p(v):=g_p(v,\cdot),$$

so that $\flat_p(v)(w)=g_p(v,w)$; it is $\mathbb R$-linear by bilinearity of
$g_p$. Its kernel is $\{v:g_p(v,w)=0\text{ for all }w\}=\{0\}$ because $g_p$ is
nondegenerate, and $\dim_{\mathbb R}T_pM=\dim_{\mathbb R}T_p^*M=4$ since the
coordinate derivations of a chart form a basis of $T_pM$
([[thm-coordinate-derivations-form-a-basis-of-the-tangent-space]]); hence
$\flat_p$ is a linear isomorphism and has an inverse
$\sharp_p:T_p^*M\to T_pM$.

**Inverse metric.** The **inverse metric** at $p$ is the symmetric bilinear form

$$g_p^{-1}:T_p^*M\times T_p^*M\longrightarrow\mathbb R,\qquad g_p^{-1}(\alpha,\beta):=g_p(\sharp_p\alpha,\sharp_p\beta).$$

It is symmetric because $g_p$ is, and it is nondegenerate: if
$g_p^{-1}(\alpha,\beta)=0$ for all $\beta$, then $g_p(\sharp_p\alpha,\cdot)=0$,
so $\sharp_p\alpha=0$ and hence $\alpha=0$.

**Components in a chart.** Let $(U,x)$ be a smooth chart and
$g_{ab}(q)=g_q(\partial_a|_q,\partial_b|_q)$ the components of $g$; let
$dx^a|_q$ be the differential of the coordinate function $x^a$ at $q$
([[def-differential-of-a-smooth-map]]), so that
$dx^a|_q(\partial_b|_q)=\partial_b|_q(x^a)=\delta^a{}_b$. Define the components
of the inverse metric in this chart by

$$g^{ab}(q):=g_q^{-1}\bigl(dx^a|_q,\,dx^b|_q\bigr),\qquad q\in U,$$

so that $\sharp_q(dx^a|_q)=\sum_bg^{ab}(q)\,\partial_b|_q$; equivalently
$(g^{ab}(q))$ is the inverse matrix of $(g_{ab}(q))$ at every $q$, that is

$$g^{ac}(q)\,g_{cb}(q)=\delta^a{}_b=\delta^c{}_bg^{ab}(q),$$

because $g_q(\sharp_qdx^a|_q,\partial_c|_q)=dx^a|_q(\partial_c|_q)=\delta^a{}_c$
and also $g_q(\sharp_qdx^a|_q,\partial_c|_q)=\sum_bg^{ab}(q)g_{bc}(q)$. In
particular $g^{ab}=g^{ba}$. The components $g^{ab}$ depend smoothly on $q$;
this is proved in [[lem-gr-inverse-metric-is-smooth]].

**Raising, lowering and metric trace.** Let $A$ be a smooth symmetric covariant
$2$-tensor field on an open set $V\subseteq M$
([[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]]). At each $p\in V$ define the
endomorphism

$$A^\sharp_p:T_pM\to T_pM,\qquad A^\sharp_p(v):=\sharp_p\bigl(A_p(v,\cdot)\bigr),$$

characterized by $g_p(A^\sharp_p(v),w)=A_p(v,w)$ for all $w\in T_pM$; it is
self-adjoint for $g_p$ because $A_p$ is symmetric. Its **metric trace** is

$$\operatorname{tr}_g(A)(p):=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(A^\sharp_p\bigr)$$

with the trace of an endomorphism as in [[def-trace-of-an-endomorphism]]. In a
chart the raised, mixed and doubly raised components are

$$A^{ab}:=g^{ac}g^{bd}A_{cd},\qquad A^a{}_b:=g^{ac}A_{cb},\qquad\text{and}\qquad \operatorname{tr}_g(A)=g^{ab}A_{ab},$$

the last identity obtained by evaluating in a $g_p$-orthonormal basis
$(e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$, where $g_p(e_a,e_b)=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)_{ab}$ by
[[lem-timelike-cone-has-two-convex-components]] so that
$g^{ab}A_{ab}=\sum_a g^{aa}A_{aa}=-A(e_0,e_0)+A(e_1,e_1)+A(e_2,e_2)+A(e_3,e_3)$,
which is the trace of the endomorphism $v\mapsto\sharp_p(A_p(v,\cdot))$ in that
basis. All these operations are pointwise and depend only on $g$, $A$ and the
duality pairing, not on a chart.

**Conventions.** Raising and lowering apply to one index at a time and preserve
index order; $A_{ab}$, $A^a{}_b$ and $A^{ab}$ denote the same tensor $A$ with
indices positioned by $g$. The musical isomorphisms and the inverse metric are
defined for every smooth Lorentzian four-manifold of this library; no choice
principle is used in this definition, every ingredient being pointwise linear
algebra over $\mathbb R$ together with the pointwise nondegeneracy of $g_p$.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]) and let $\nabla$ be an affine connection
on $M$ ([[def-affine-connection-on-a-smooth-manifold]]). Smooth vector fields
are smooth sections of the tangent bundle
([[def-smooth-vector-field-as-a-tangent-bundle-section]]); as there, their use
rests on the canonical smooth structure of $TM$, which assumes the axiom
$\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ of [[def-countable-choice]]. This is the only use of that
axiom in this definition.

**(a) Metric compatibility.** The connection $\nabla$ is **$g$-compatible**, or
**compatible with the metric** $g$, when for all smooth vector fields $X,Y,Z$ on
$M$ the identity of smooth functions

$$X\bigl(g(Y,Z)\bigr)=g(\nabla_XY,Z)+g(Y,\nabla_XZ)$$

holds on $M$. Here $g(Y,Z)$ is the smooth function $p\mapsto g_p(Y_p,Z_p)$ and
$X$ acts on functions as a derivation; the identity uses only the action of
$\nabla$ on vector fields and requires no extension of $\nabla$ to tensor
fields. When such an extension is available, this identity is the statement
$\nabla_Xg=0$, and the compatibility of $\nabla$ with the inverse metric
$g^{-1}$ follows; neither statement is part of this definition.

**(b) Torsion freedom.** The **torsion** of $\nabla$ is the tangent-valued
$2$-tensor $T(X,Y)=\nabla_XY-\nabla_YX-[X,Y]$ of
[[def-torsion-tensor-of-an-affine-connection]], with bracket as in
[[def-lie-bracket-of-smooth-vector-fields]]. The connection is **torsion-free**
when $T(X,Y)=0$ for all smooth $X,Y$, that is, when
$\nabla_XY-\nabla_YX=[X,Y]$ identically.

**(c) Metric-selected connections.** A **metric-selected connection** for
$(M,g)$ is an affine connection on $M$ that is both torsion-free and
$g$-compatible. Equivalently, it is an element of the class

$$\operatorname{LC}(M,g):=\{\nabla:\nabla\text{ is an affine connection on }M,\ \nabla\text{ is torsion-free and }g\text{-compatible}\}.$$

The name records that the pair of conditions selects the connection out of all
affine connections; it is the pair of conditions imposed on the connection that
conventional general relativity uses, and the connection so selected is called
the **Levi–Civita connection** of $g$.

Let $M$ be a smooth four-manifold without boundary and let $g$ be a smooth
symmetric covariant $2$-tensor field on $M$ such that $g_p$ is nondegenerate at
every $p\in M$ ([[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]],
[[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]]). This holds in particular
when $(M,g,N)$ is a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold and $g$ is
its metric ([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]). For smooth vector fields
$X,Y,Z$ put

$$K(X,Y,Z):=X\bigl(g(Y,Z)\bigr)+Y\bigl(g(Z,X)\bigr)-Z\bigl(g(X,Y)\bigr)+g([X,Y],Z)+g([Z,X],Y)-g([Y,Z],X),$$

with brackets as in [[def-lie-bracket-of-smooth-vector-fields]].

**(a) Existence and formulas.** There is exactly one affine connection
$\nabla$ on $M$ ([[def-affine-connection-on-a-smooth-manifold]]) satisfying

$$2g(\nabla_XY,Z)=K(X,Y,Z)\qquad\text{for all smooth }X,Y,Z .$$

It is torsion-free and $g$-compatible, so it is a metric-selected connection
for $(M,g)$ ([[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]]); in every smooth chart its
Christoffel symbols are

$$\Gamma^a{}_{bc}=\tfrac12\,g^{ad}\bigl(\partial_bg_{dc}+\partial_cg_{bd}-\partial_dg_{bc}\bigr),$$

with $g^{ad}$ the inverse-metric components
([[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]],
[[def-christoffel-symbols-of-an-affine-connection]]).

**(b) Uniqueness.** If an affine connection $\nabla'$ on $M$ is torsion-free
and $g$-compatible, then $\nabla'=\nabla$. Consequently the class
$\operatorname{LC}(M,g)$ of metric-selected connections has exactly one
element; it is the **Levi–Civita connection** of $g$.

**(c) Induced derivative on tensor fields.** Let $\nabla^*$ be the dual
connection on $T^*M$ and let the product connection of
[[def-product-connection-on-tensor-and-hom-bundles]] act on the tensor bundles
of [[def-gr-tensor-fields-and-components]]. Then, in every smooth chart, for
every smooth tensor field $T$ of type $(r,s)$,

$$T^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s;c}=\partial_cT^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s}+\sum_{i=1}^{r}\Gamma^{a_i}{}_{dc}\,T^{a_1\cdots d\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s}-\sum_{j=1}^{s}\Gamma^{d}{}_{b_jc}\,T^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots d\cdots b_s},$$

where the slot marked $d$ replaces the named index; this derivative commutes
with every contraction in the sense of [[def-contraction-of-a-mixed-tensor]],
and it annihilates the metric and the inverse metric:

$$g_{ab;c}=0,\qquad g^{ab}{}_{;c}=0 .$$

([[def-gr-dust-matter-model]]). Then

metric-selected connection $\nabla$ ([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]) and let
$U\subseteq M$ be a nonempty open matter domain
([[prop-an-open-subset-of-a-smooth-manifold-has-a-canonical-restricted-smooth-structure]]).

**(a) Data.** A **perfect-fluid model** on $U$ is a triple $(\varepsilon,p,n)$
consisting of two smooth functions $\varepsilon,p:U\to\mathbb R$, the **rest
energy density** and the **pressure**, and a smooth future-directed unit
timelike vector field $n$ on $U$ with $g_p(n_p,n_p)=-1$ and
$g_p(n_p,N_p)<0$ at every $p$ ([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],

$\varepsilon(U)\subseteq D_P$, together with the relation $p=P(\varepsilon)$;
the relation is a further assumption and is not part of the basic triple.

**stress-energy tensor** is

$$T^{ab}:=(\varepsilon+p)n^an^b+p\,g^{ab},$$

and the **rest-space projection** is the smooth tensor field

$$h^{ab}:=g^{ab}+n^an^b .$$

and pressure, and their units, are fixed by the framework's matter postulate,
not by this definition.

$$D\varepsilon+(\varepsilon+p)\vartheta=0,\qquad (\varepsilon+p)a^b+h^{ba}\partial_ap=0 .$$

equations hold is proved in
[[prop-gr-dust-and-perfect-fluid-conservation-equations]]; the definition
asserts neither divergence-freedom nor the equations.

set $U\subseteq M$ and let $h$ be a smooth symmetric covariant $2$-tensor on
$U$. The derivative at $\hat g$ in the direction $h$ of the operator
$g\mapsto\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}[g]-\bar\nabla_{(a}H_{b)}[g]$ equals
$$-\tfrac12\hat g^{cd}\,\bar\nabla_c\bar\nabla_d h_{ab}+L_{ab}(h,\bar\nabla h;\hat g,\bar g),$$
where $L$ is a smooth expression linear in $h$ and its first
$\bar\nabla$-derivatives with coefficients built from $\hat g,\hat g^{-1},\bar g$
and the background curvature. In particular the principal symbol is
$-\tfrac12\hat g^{cd}\xi_c\xi_d$ times the identity on the metric slot at every
covector $\xi$.

**(b) [first-order reduction]** Fix a chart $(x^0,x^1,x^2,x^3)$ with
$x^0=t$. Introduce the metric variables
$$u:=\bigl(g_{ab},\ p_{ab}:=\bar\nabla_0g_{ab},\ q_{abi}:=\bar\nabla_ig_{ab}\bigr)$$
(symmetry in $a,b$ understood) and the relation variables $\bar\nabla_0g_{ab}-p_{ab}=0$ and $\bar\nabla_0q_{abi}-\bar\nabla_ip_{ab}=\mathcal C_{abi}$, where $\mathcal C_{abi}=-\bar R^c{}_{a0i}g_{cb}-\bar R^c{}_{b0i}g_{ac}$. and the resulting first-order system for $u$ is symmetric hyperbolic on every
region where $g^{00}<0$ and the spatial block $(g^{ij})$ is positive definite:
the coefficient of $\bar\nabla_0u$ is the block diagonal
$\operatorname{diag}(I,-g^{00}I,g^{ij}I)$ (on the three slots
$g,p,q$), which is positive definite there, and the coefficients of the spatial
derivatives are symmetric.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold and let
$p\in M$ ([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]). The cotangent space $T_p^*M$ is
the algebraic dual of $T_pM$ ([[def-algebraic-dual-and-linear-functional]]).

**Musical isomorphisms.** Define the **flat map**

$$\flat_p:T_pM\longrightarrow T_p^*M,\qquad \flat_p(v):=g_p(v,\cdot),$$

so that $\flat_p(v)(w)=g_p(v,w)$; it is $\mathbb R$-linear by bilinearity of
$g_p$. Its kernel is $\{v:g_p(v,w)=0\text{ for all }w\}=\{0\}$ because $g_p$ is
nondegenerate, and $\dim_{\mathbb R}T_pM=\dim_{\mathbb R}T_p^*M=4$ since the
coordinate derivations of a chart form a basis of $T_pM$
([[thm-coordinate-derivations-form-a-basis-of-the-tangent-space]]); hence
$\flat_p$ is a linear isomorphism and has an inverse
$\sharp_p:T_p^*M\to T_pM$.

**Inverse metric.** The **inverse metric** at $p$ is the symmetric bilinear form

$$g_p^{-1}:T_p^*M\times T_p^*M\longrightarrow\mathbb R,\qquad g_p^{-1}(\alpha,\beta):=g_p(\sharp_p\alpha,\sharp_p\beta).$$

It is symmetric because $g_p$ is, and it is nondegenerate: if
$g_p^{-1}(\alpha,\beta)=0$ for all $\beta$, then $g_p(\sharp_p\alpha,\cdot)=0$,
so $\sharp_p\alpha=0$ and hence $\alpha=0$.

**Components in a chart.** Let $(U,x)$ be a smooth chart and
$g_{ab}(q)=g_q(\partial_a|_q,\partial_b|_q)$ the components of $g$; let
$dx^a|_q$ be the differential of the coordinate function $x^a$ at $q$
([[def-differential-of-a-smooth-map]]), so that
$dx^a|_q(\partial_b|_q)=\partial_b|_q(x^a)=\delta^a{}_b$. Define the components
of the inverse metric in this chart by

$$g^{ab}(q):=g_q^{-1}\bigl(dx^a|_q,\,dx^b|_q\bigr),\qquad q\in U,$$

so that $\sharp_q(dx^a|_q)=\sum_bg^{ab}(q)\,\partial_b|_q$; equivalently
$(g^{ab}(q))$ is the inverse matrix of $(g_{ab}(q))$ at every $q$, that is

$$g^{ac}(q)\,g_{cb}(q)=\delta^a{}_b=\delta^c{}_bg^{ab}(q),$$

because $g_q(\sharp_qdx^a|_q,\partial_c|_q)=dx^a|_q(\partial_c|_q)=\delta^a{}_c$
and also $g_q(\sharp_qdx^a|_q,\partial_c|_q)=\sum_bg^{ab}(q)g_{bc}(q)$. In
particular $g^{ab}=g^{ba}$. The components $g^{ab}$ depend smoothly on $q$;
this is proved in [[lem-gr-inverse-metric-is-smooth]].

**Raising, lowering and metric trace.** Let $A$ be a smooth symmetric covariant
$2$-tensor field on an open set $V\subseteq M$
([[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]]). At each $p\in V$ define the
endomorphism

$$A^\sharp_p:T_pM\to T_pM,\qquad A^\sharp_p(v):=\sharp_p\bigl(A_p(v,\cdot)\bigr),$$

characterized by $g_p(A^\sharp_p(v),w)=A_p(v,w)$ for all $w\in T_pM$; it is
self-adjoint for $g_p$ because $A_p$ is symmetric. Its **metric trace** is

$$\operatorname{tr}_g(A)(p):=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(A^\sharp_p\bigr)$$

with the trace of an endomorphism as in [[def-trace-of-an-endomorphism]]. In a
chart the raised, mixed and doubly raised components are

$$A^{ab}:=g^{ac}g^{bd}A_{cd},\qquad A^a{}_b:=g^{ac}A_{cb},\qquad\text{and}\qquad \operatorname{tr}_g(A)=g^{ab}A_{ab},$$

the last identity obtained by evaluating in a $g_p$-orthonormal basis
$(e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$, where $g_p(e_a,e_b)=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)_{ab}$ by
[[lem-timelike-cone-has-two-convex-components]] so that
$g^{ab}A_{ab}=\sum_a g^{aa}A_{aa}=-A(e_0,e_0)+A(e_1,e_1)+A(e_2,e_2)+A(e_3,e_3)$,
which is the trace of the endomorphism $v\mapsto\sharp_p(A_p(v,\cdot))$ in that
basis. All these operations are pointwise and depend only on $g$, $A$ and the
duality pairing, not on a chart.

**Conventions.** Raising and lowering apply to one index at a time and preserve
index order; $A_{ab}$, $A^a{}_b$ and $A^{ab}$ denote the same tensor $A$ with
indices positioned by $g$. The musical isomorphisms and the inverse metric are
defined for every smooth Lorentzian four-manifold of this library; no choice
principle is used in this definition, every ingredient being pointwise linear
algebra over $\mathbb R$ together with the pointwise nondegeneracy of $g_p$.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]) and let $\nabla$ be an affine connection
on $M$ ([[def-affine-connection-on-a-smooth-manifold]]). Smooth vector fields
are smooth sections of the tangent bundle
([[def-smooth-vector-field-as-a-tangent-bundle-section]]); as there, their use
rests on the canonical smooth structure of $TM$, which assumes the axiom
$\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ of [[def-countable-choice]]. This is the only use of that
axiom in this definition.

**(a) Metric compatibility.** The connection $\nabla$ is **$g$-compatible**, or
**compatible with the metric** $g$, when for all smooth vector fields $X,Y,Z$ on
$M$ the identity of smooth functions

$$X\bigl(g(Y,Z)\bigr)=g(\nabla_XY,Z)+g(Y,\nabla_XZ)$$

holds on $M$. Here $g(Y,Z)$ is the smooth function $p\mapsto g_p(Y_p,Z_p)$ and
$X$ acts on functions as a derivation; the identity uses only the action of
$\nabla$ on vector fields and requires no extension of $\nabla$ to tensor
fields. When such an extension is available, this identity is the statement
$\nabla_Xg=0$, and the compatibility of $\nabla$ with the inverse metric
$g^{-1}$ follows; neither statement is part of this definition.

**(b) Torsion freedom.** The **torsion** of $\nabla$ is the tangent-valued
$2$-tensor $T(X,Y)=\nabla_XY-\nabla_YX-[X,Y]$ of
[[def-torsion-tensor-of-an-affine-connection]], with bracket as in
[[def-lie-bracket-of-smooth-vector-fields]]. The connection is **torsion-free**
when $T(X,Y)=0$ for all smooth $X,Y$, that is, when
$\nabla_XY-\nabla_YX=[X,Y]$ identically.

**(c) Metric-selected connections.** A **metric-selected connection** for
$(M,g)$ is an affine connection on $M$ that is both torsion-free and
$g$-compatible. Equivalently, it is an element of the class

$$\operatorname{LC}(M,g):=\{\nabla:\nabla\text{ is an affine connection on }M,\ \nabla\text{ is torsion-free and }g\text{-compatible}\}.$$

The name records that the pair of conditions selects the connection out of all
affine connections; it is the pair of conditions imposed on the connection that
conventional general relativity uses, and the connection so selected is called
the **Levi–Civita connection** of $g$.
